Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear questions. Below is our recommended path and the tradeoffs so procurement has what it needs to decide quickly.

Short answer (recommended): Commit to the Growth profile — a 24-GPU minimum floor with a staged three-month ramp. Why: it balances predictable latency for your latency-sensitive endpoints and avoids the full cost of a 48-GPU anchor until volume validates it.

Sizing & latency rationale:
- 24-GPU floor: with Redwood's continuous batching + KV prefix caching enabled and a 2x warm standby buffer for hot endpoints, we've observed p99 latency in target workloads similar to yours at 75–80% of your peak traffic. That maps to a 99% SLO in our benchmarks for mixed batch/stream patterns.
- 12-GPU floor: acceptable for early pilot, but risk of p99 regressions under spikes and longer tail latency during sustained bursts; requires aggressive burst credits and more frequent autoscale to maintain SLOs.
- 48-GPU floor: will hit SLOs comfortably with headroom and lowest per-token cost, but increases committed spend significantly. Good if you want a predictable low unit cost from day one.

Suggested ramp schedule (example):
- Month 1: Activate 30% of ramp (initial 7–8 GPUs effectively in active lanes; remainder warm). Monitoring gates at two weeks.
- Month 2: Move to 70% active (apply additional capacity and enable burst lanes).
- Month 3: Full activation to 100% committed floor + autoscale to support peak bursts.

Fallback & decommit path:
- If usage doesn't track to plan within the first 60 days, we offer a 30-day grace decommit review window and a one-time 10% credit toward the next quarter's invoice if you choose to hold at a lower floor. We also provide temporary burst credits for spikes during month 1 at no extra charge to reduce activation risk.

Pricing delta (illustrative):
- 12-GPU soft-floor: list unit $X.XX / 1k tokens; committed discount baseline = -10%
- 24-GPU growth-floor: list unit $Y.YY / 1k tokens; committed discount baseline = -18% (approx 12–15% cheaper per token vs 12GPU)
- 48-GPU anchor-floor: list unit $Z.ZZ / 1k tokens; committed discount baseline = -28% (approx 20–25% cheaper per token vs 24GPU)

Attached: revised committed quote for 24-GPU floor (redwood-revised-quote-24gpu.pdf) and the MOP with expected perf numbers (pinebrook_mop_v3.xlsx).

3) Week 0–4: pilot traffic + monitoring; we will provide a weekly dashboard and one ops call per week.
